# Scoped synchronous glob adapter

This local package replaces only the `fast-glob` dependency of `@next/eslint-plugin-next` and `vite-plugin-dynamic-import`. It delegates matching and walking to the pinned `glob@13.0.6` package. It does not implement the full fast-glob API.

Supported contract: CommonJS and ESM `sync` / `globSync`, string or string-array patterns, and the `cwd` and `onlyDirectories` options used by those two consumers. Other options fail explicitly. Ordinary wildcards, globstars, character classes, exclusions, and brace alternatives such as `*.{js,ts}` are supported. Brace ranges (numeric and alphabetic, including padded and stepped forms), extglobs, and unclosed character classes are rejected explicitly with `ERR_GLOB_UNSUPPORTED_PATTERN`; these constructs are not generated by the project's dynamic-import integration. Async calls, streams, filesystem injection, and task generation are intentionally unsupported.

Directory patterns are not automatically expanded; ordinary searches include files only, exclude implicit dot entries, match case sensitively, and follow symlinks. The adapter preserves static path spelling, dynamic directory trailing-slash behavior, leading `./`, absolute results, exclusions, and the traversal-base behavior of trailing `/**`. `onlyDirectories` uses glob's documented trailing-slash matching, which includes directory symlinks. Result ordering is not guaranteed, as with upstream fast-glob.

Inputs are limited to 128 patterns, 4,096 characters each, 32,768 total characters, 16 nested groups, a conservative 4,096 branch-product budget, and two separate `*` runs per path segment. Adjacent `**` counts as one run. Excessive patterns throw `TypeError` with `ERR_GLOB_PATTERN_LIMIT` before the matcher or directory traversal runs. This also rejects the independently reproduced `*a` repetition backtracking case; repeated extglobs are rejected altogether. These limits address the observed problematic cases, not every possible adversarial glob input.

`tests/glob-compat.test.mjs` checks an upstream fixture baseline and executes the installed consumers' actual source with the adapter. The baseline was captured before removing upstream fast-glob and does not add it as a production or test dependency.

References: [glob documentation and source](https://github.com/isaacs/node-glob), [fast-glob behavior](https://github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob).
